transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, after some long days on the job site, I'll come home and... I just end up eating way more than I meant to. Like, leftover takeout, chips, cereal... whatever is around, really. I just kind of keep going until I'm... uncomfortably full. So... yeah. That's mostly it.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset before these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

Um... I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't really paid attention to that. Work is just work, you know? I guess I'm mostly just tired by the time I get in. I wouldn't really say I feel upset or anything like that.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started, or do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating during those times?

Um... I guess... it's hard to stop. Once I start on those evenings, it kind of just feels like I'm on autopilot. I'll be telling myself to stop, you know, because I have an early crew start the next morning, but... I still end up going back to the kitchen for more. So... yeah.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating like that?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't really dwell on it. I usually just... try to go to sleep, honestly, so I can be up for my shift. I haven't really thought about whether I feel guilty or not.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in sex recently?
Um... no, not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. It's just... normal, I guess.
Do you think your eating more than you meant to is ever triggered by feeling stressed, anxious, or upset?
Um... I don't know. I guess I haven't really paid attention to what triggers it. I just... I just eat sometimes. I don't think it's tied to being upset or anything. It just happens.
Do you think your eating more than you meant to has anything to do with your sex life?
Um... no. I don't really see how that would be connected. So, no... it doesn't have anything to do with that.
Do you think you eat more than you meant to because you're not interested in sex at those times?
Um... no. I really don't think so. Like I said, they just... they aren't connected for me.
Do you think you eat more than you meant to when you're not in the mood for sex?
No... I mean, I really don't. Like I just said, it has nothing to do with that at all. I'm not sure why we keep coming back to it.
Do you think you eat more than you meant to because you're using food as a way to cope with a low sex drive?
Look... no. It's just not about that. I really don't know what else to tell you about it.
Do you think there's any connection between your eating and your sexual activity?
No. I... I really don't. I've already said no to this. There is zero connection. Can we please just move on to something else?
Do you often lose your appetite for food when you're not in the mood for sex?
No. I... I don't. Like I've been saying, my appetite and... that... they just aren't related. At all. I don't know why we're still on this.
Do you think your lack of interest in sex contributes to your eating more than you meant to?
No. I don't. I... I really just want to talk about something else now. I've answered this.
Do you think there's anything else, besides being tired from work, that contributes to your eating more than you meant to?
I don't... I don't really know. Just stress, I guess. I mean, work is a lot, but... no, I can't really think of anything else specific.
Do you ever eat more than you meant to after having sex?
No. I... look, I thought we were moving on from this. Like I said, they just aren't connected for me. So... no. I don't.
Do you ever feel sexually satisfied after eating more than you meant to?
No. I... I really don't want to talk about sex anymore. I've said they aren't connected. I just... no.
Do you think you eat more than you meant to when you're feeling emotionally numb or detached?
I don't think so. I... I just feel stressed. I wouldn't say numb. Just... stressed.
Do you think you eat more than you meant to as a way to deal with stress?
I don't... I don't really think so. It's not like it helps. It just... happens. I wouldn't call it a way to deal with anything.
Do you think your eating more than you meant to is ever related to not feeling like having sex?
I... I thought I just said I don't want to talk about that anymore. No. It has nothing to do with that.
Do you think your eating more than you meant to is related to a decrease in your desire for sex?
I... I literally just answered that. No. It's not related to that at all. Can we please just drop it?
